title: Routing
description: Domains, APIs, sockets and operations that something other than the mock answers: a service at a URL, or a function passed in code. Per-environment configuration, read at boot; never part of a contract set.

Route.description: One domain, API or operation, and who answers it: exactly one of domain, api and operation, and one of to and handler.

domain.description: A domain the contracts declare, by the name of its directory, or * for every domain. Every route its APIs declare, and every event their state machines receive, is routed. With *, so is a request for a route the mock doesn't have, and any entry naming a domain, API or operation overrides it.

api.description: An API the contracts declare, by name: its OpenAPI file's name without -openapi.yaml, which its events AsyncAPI shares. Every route it declares, and every event its state machines receive, is routed. Overrides a domain entry for that API. Or a socket: an AsyncAPI document reached over its own connection, which the mock serves at its localhost server, by its file name without -asyncapi.yaml. Only an entry naming a socket routes it; it takes no except or includeHeaders, and no operation entry names one of its operations, since its messages all travel on one connection.

operation.description: One operation, by id: an OpenAPI operationId, or an AsyncAPI receive operation's. Bare when one API declares it, $apis.<api>.<id> when more than one does. Overrides a domain or API entry for that operation.

except.description: What stays in the mock, inside this entry: on a domain, an API in it or an operation; on *, any API or operation; on an API, an operation in it. Not on an operation entry.

to.description: Absolute base URL of the service that answers. For a request, its path is a prefix: the request's own path is appended to it. A received event is POSTed to it as written, in the CloudEvents HTTP binding's structured mode. A socket's connections are opened to it as written, passing on the subprotocols the client offered; it may be ws or wss, and http or https is taken as ws or wss, as the WebSocket constructor takes it. Only a socket is routed to a ws or wss URL. May not carry a username or password: this file is configuration, and a credential belongs to the target, or to a header the caller sends and includeHeaders names.

handler.description: A function that answers instead, passed in code only, so never in a file. For a domain, API or operation, it has fetch's signature, (Request) => Response; a received event reaches it as the request to would have been sent, and what it answers is checked against the operation's response schema. For a socket, it has the WebSocket constructor's signature, used as new handler(url, protocols), and every message it sends is checked against the messages the contract lets the socket send.

includeHeaders.description: Headers to pass along beyond the default set, in either direction. Anything not named here or in the default set is dropped, credentials included. Not on a socket: a browser's WebSocket sends no headers of its own, and its subprotocols, a token among them, are passed on as offered.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the service before answering 504, or, for a socket, for its connection to open before closing the client's with 1014. Defaults to 10000.
